text:
**Short answer: about 300-400 W of solar refills a 1,000 Wh station in one sunny day. A 200 W panel works too, but it takes about 1.5 days.**

**The math**
- Daily energy is roughly panel watts × peak sun hours × 0.7-0.75. Real panels lose output to heat, angle, and charging losses.
- At 4.5 peak sun hours, a 200 W panel gives about 630 Wh/day, so a 1,000 Wh station refills in about 1.5 days ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- For a full recharge in one day, the estimates are:

| Conditions | Panel watts for 1,000 Wh in one day |
|---|---|
| Good summer sun (5 peak sun hours) | about 270-300 W |
| 4 peak sun hours | about 340 W |
| Northern winter (2 peak sun hours) | about 735 W |

These figures come from [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/) and [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/).

- A quick rule of thumb is battery Wh ÷ 5 ≈ 200 W for about a day and a half of decent sun ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

**Before you buy**
- **Check your station's maximum solar input.** If it caps at 200 W, a 400 W array won't charge faster, though it will hold that cap longer in weak light ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
- **Check the input voltage range.** Panels wired in series add voltage, and exceeding the station's limit can damage it.
- **Expect slower charging if you're using the station at the same time.** Net charge is solar input minus your load.

**A product option**
If your station accepts about 400 W, the [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel) is $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26. That's enough for a one-day refill in decent sun.
